zh.q: 空气里到处是氮气，为什么还要建这么大一座厂才能变成氨？
zh.concl: 反应可逆、放热、气体分子数减少：要同时照顾「快」和「多」，所以拆成五个工段（见下方面包屑）。
points: 总式左边没有现成原料：H₂ 靠 CH₄ 与水蒸气转化，N₂ 靠空气液化分馏。
反应可逆、放热、气体分子数减少：想「多」要低温高压，想「快」要高温和铁触媒。
两个要求打架，工程上只能折中，折出一条五段流水线。

zh.q: 为什么第一件事是把原料气洗干净？
zh.concl: 原料气里的硫等杂质会让铁触媒中毒，有的中毒不可逆；所以先脱硫、变换、脱碳
points: 硫、磷、砷、氯是永久毒物，中毒后不可恢复；H₂O、CO、CO₂、O₂ 是暂时毒物。
变换反应一举两得：把 CO 变成 CO₂ 除掉，同时多产一份 H₂。
脱碳还防低温段干冰堵塞，也防 CO₂ 稀释气体、拖慢反应。

zh.q: 为什么要把压力压到几十个大气压？
zh.concl: 反应后气体分子数减少，加压使平衡右移、速率加快；但压力越高，设备和能耗越贵，所以取 10–30 MPa
points: 为什么不再高：塔壁应力大、厚壁设备造价高、压缩功耗电，还要防氢脆。
先净化后压缩：否则杂质被一起压缩，多耗能，触媒照样中毒。

zh.q: 温度越低平衡越好，为什么偏要 400～500 ℃？
zh.concl: 低温平衡好但反应太慢；高温快但平衡差；铁触媒在 400–500 ℃ 活性最好，这是折中
points: 放热 + 气体分子数减少：低温高压对平衡有利（200 ℃、100 MPa 可达 98.8 %）。
但温度低速率太慢、铁触媒 400 ℃ 以下几乎没活性，所以折中取 400～500 ℃。
催化剂只加快到达平衡，不改变平衡转化率，也不改变 ΔH。

zh.q: 合成塔里面长什么样，热是怎么压住的？
zh.concl: 塔内分四段催化床，段间打入冷激气控温，避免烧坏触媒；催化剂只加快速率，不改变平衡
points: 合成塔通常分 4 段催化床，段间打入冷激气，把床层温升压住。
放热反应：不控温，床层会一路飞升，铁晶粒再结晶长大、活性下降。
催化剂只加快到达平衡；床层怎么分段都不改变平衡转化率。

zh.q: 每次只转化一小部分，为什么总利用率能到 97 %？
zh.concl: 冷却分出液氨，未反应的 N₂、H₂ 送回去再反应；它提高的是原料利用率，不是平衡转化率。
points: 单程只有约 15 %，不分离循环就等于把大部分原料放空。
氨容易液化（沸点很低），所以「加压 + 降温」两条路都能把它变成液体。
循环把原料利用率提到约 97 %，但平衡转化率一点没变。

zh.q: 考核：你来当班长——能不能把产率稳住，又不出事故？
zh.concl: 考核没有新结论：把前面六步的条件同时照顾到——温度、压力落在教材区间，净化与循环都开着。
points: 温度、压强都要落在教材区间：400–500 ℃、10–30 MPa。
产率靠「条件 + 触媒活性 + 循环」一起撑：任一处掉链子，读数立刻掉。
越界就有代价：床层 640 ℃ 或系统 38 MPa 会走「倒计时 → 事故 → 复盘」。

en.q: Nitrogen is everywhere in the air. Why does it take such a huge plant to turn it into ammonia?
en.concl: Reversible, exothermic, fewer gas molecules: to look after both "fast" and "more" it is split into five sections (see the breadcrumb below).
points: The left side of the overall equation has no ready-made feedstock: H₂ comes from reforming CH₄ with steam, N₂ from liquefying and fractionating air.
The reaction is reversible, exothermic and reduces the number of gas molecules: "more" needs low temperature and high pressure, "faster" needs high temperature and an iron catalyst.
The two demands conflict, so engineering compromises, and the compromise becomes a five-section line.

en.q: Why is the first job to clean the feed gas?
en.concl: Sulfur and other impurities in the feed gas poison the iron catalyst, some irreversibly; so desulfurize, shift and decarbonize first
points: Sulfur, phosphorus, arsenic and chlorine are permanent poisons, with no recovery; H₂O, CO, CO₂ and O₂ are temporary poisons.
The shift reaction does two jobs: it turns CO into CO₂ to be removed, and makes an extra share of H₂.
Decarbonization also prevents dry ice blocking the cold sections, and stops CO₂ diluting the gas and slowing the reaction.

en.q: Why squeeze the pressure up to hundreds of atmospheres?
en.concl: The reaction reduces the number of gas molecules, so pressure shifts the equilibrium right and speeds it up; but the higher the pressure, the costlier the equipment and energy, so 10–30 MPa is used
points: Textbook data table (400 ℃): 10 MPa 25.1 % → 30 MPa 47.0 % → 60 MPa 65.2 %, diminishing returns.
Why not higher: large stress in the tower wall, costly thick-walled equipment, compression consumes power, and hydrogen embrittlement must be prevented.
Purify before compressing: otherwise the impurities are compressed too, wasting energy, and the catalyst is still poisoned.

en.q: Lower temperature means better equilibrium. Why insist on 400–500 ℃?
en.concl: Low temperature gives better equilibrium but too slow a reaction; high temperature is fast but the equilibrium is poor; the iron catalyst works best at 400–500 ℃, which is the compromise
points: Exothermic + fewer gas molecules: low temperature and high pressure favor equilibrium (200 ℃ and 100 MPa reach 98.8 %).
But at low temperature the rate is too slow and the iron catalyst is almost inactive below 400 ℃, so the compromise is 400–500 ℃.
A catalyst only speeds up reaching equilibrium; it does not change the equilibrium conversion or ΔH.

en.q: What does the inside of the synthesis tower look like, and how is the heat kept down?
en.concl: The tower has four catalyst beds with quench gas between them to control temperature and avoid burning out the catalyst; the catalyst only speeds up the rate and does not change the equilibrium
points: A synthesis tower usually has 4 catalyst beds, with quench gas injected between them to hold down the temperature rise.
Exothermic reaction: without temperature control the beds keep heating up, iron grains recrystallize and grow, and activity falls.
A catalyst only speeds up reaching equilibrium; however the beds are split, the equilibrium conversion does not change.

en.q: Each pass converts only a small part. How does total utilization reach 97 %?
en.concl: Cooling separates liquid ammonia, and unreacted N₂ and H₂ are sent back to react again; this raises feed utilization, not equilibrium conversion.
points: A single pass converts only about 15 %; without separation and recycling most of the feed is vented.
Ammonia liquefies easily (low boiling point), so both "pressure" and "cooling" can turn it into a liquid.
Recycling raises feed utilization to about 97 %, but the equilibrium conversion does not change at all.

en.q: Assessment: you are the shift leader. Can you hold output steady without an accident?
en.concl: The assessment has no new conclusion: look after the conditions of the previous six steps at the same time: temperature and pressure within the textbook ranges, purification and recycle both on.
points: Temperature and pressure must both be within the textbook ranges: 400–500 ℃, 10–30 MPa.
Output depends on "conditions + catalyst activity + recycle" together: if any one fails, the reading drops at once.
Going out of range has a cost: bed 640 ℃ or system 38 MPa triggers "countdown → incident → review".
